headline: #Powered by Cloud Agents
summary: A Project runs on its own computer in the cloud, so closing your laptop doesn't stop it. When something needs testing on your machine, the coordinator spins up a local agent to run it there.

headline: #Shared context
summary: You shouldn't have to onboard an agent every time you start a task. Each Project maintains a set of files that sync across every cloud and local machine its agents use. Agents add research and artifacts, along with what they learn about the codebase and how you prefer work to be done. headline: #Dynamic pool scheduling
summary: My Machinesconnects a single laptop or VM to your account for personal workflows.

headline: #Run on your sandboxes
summary: Cloud agents can now execute oninfrastructure you already use, including from AWS Lambda, Coder, Cloudflare, Daytona, Modal, Namespace, Vercel, and E2B.

headline: #Computer use on Linux and Mac
summary: Self-hosted workers now support computer use on Linux and Mac. With the right desktop packages, an agent can click, type, take screenshots, and drive the browser. You can watch its desktop or take control from Cursor.

headline: #Get started
summary: SelectStart from scratchin the repo picker, then prompt the agent. In the background, Cursor creates an Origin repo for you.

headline: #Turn it into a real repo, whenever you want
summary: Once the agent's build is to your liking, click theCreate repobutton to save your work in an Origin repo. Choose a custom name or pick one of the suggested ones, then set the visibility to private or internal. You'll get a fully scaffolded Origin repo, ready to share or keep building on. Navigate to the Codebase tab to find your repo and access your project.

headline: #A live preview, right in the browser
summary: Cursor now port-forwards your cloud agent's live environment straight to your browser, so you can preview it and use tools like design mode.

headline: #Subscriptions
summary: Cursor can now monitor your PRs, watch a Slack thread, or run scheduled tasks. Cursor Agent subscribes to an event source (a thread or conversation) and wakes when something happens. Subscriptions are available for cloud agents only, for now.

headline: #Custom modes
summary: Use any skill as a Custom Mode: a skill that stays pinned in the chat. Custom modes keep agents focused on a skill - you can think about it like "always on" skills.

headline: #Subagents on their own machines
summary: Subagents can now run on their own virtual machines. Each gets an isolated copy of the project with clean context in its own cloud environment.

headline: #Origin Repos
summary: The newCodebasetab is home for Origin repos.

headline: #Bring your GitHub repos
summary: Your GitHub repos can sit alongside the ones Cursor hosts. Connect GitHub to Cursor, pick your org, and you'll see the repos you can sync. Select one and Cursor pulls it in. You choose what gets synced and can disconnect a repo at any time. Anyone with read or write access to a synced repo can view it in Cursor too.

headline: #Pull requests
summary: Every repo has pull requests. Open one to see the timeline, commits, checks, and files changed. Review the diff, leave comments, and merge.

headline: #Faster starts
summary: Cursor runs a new build of your environment regularly. When a build succeeds, it becomes the environment future agents start from. Cursor keeps warm copies ready so the next agent does not wait. Internally, our environments now boot 10x faster, with 3x faster time to first token.

headline: #More resilient agent runs
summary: When a bad commit or dependency update breaks your environment, agents keep using the last successful build. The broken build never becomes active, you are notified of the issue, and your agents keep working while you debug in the background.

headline: #Build history and debugging
summary: Each environment has aBuildstab in the Cloud Agents dashboard. You can inspect build status, logs, commit SHAs, and which build each agent run used. Agents can also inspect and manage builds using built-in tools.

headline: #Built for the bigger screen
summary: The iPad layout is rebuilt around the extra space. Sidebar chats stay pinned so you can watch several agents run at once. Split screen keeps a review open next to a chat, and file diffs render in full.

headline: #A full review surface
summary: On iPhone and iPad, the review screen now covers the full PR: comments, checks, and approvals. Add or change reviewers, read comments, and prompt the agent to resolve them. The whole path from agent output to merged PR now travels with you.

headline: #Inbox
summary: An Inbox helps you and your agents stay organized. See what's in progress, what needs your attention, and which PRs are in review.

headline: #Admin controls
summary: Admins can enable the router per team or group, restrict which optimization modes members can use, set the default mode, and allow or block underlying models.

headline: Improvements↓↑
summary: Jul 17, 2026·Changelog

headline: #Interaction improvements
summary: Cursor now responds with a plan before it begins, so you can jump in and redirect early. As it works, it updates its status so you can follow each step.

headline: #Multi-repo environment support
summary: From Slack, Cursor can now start in a named multi-repo environment instead of a single default repository. If your frontend, backend, and shared code live in separate repos, Cursor reads your request and targets the environment that gives it access to all of them.

headline: #Cross-channel workflows
summary: Cursor can now read from and send messages to other Slack channels and threads. During a task, it can pull context from elsewhere in the workspace and post updates back in the original thread or the relevant channel.

headline: #Side chats
summary: Open a side chat to ask questions, explore ideas, and investigate tangents without interrupting your main agent conversation. Use/side,/btw, or the plus button at the top of the chat panel to create a new side chat that has context from the main chat.
